nora: Quick report: converting Llama->Mistral for bench run and saw subtle synth-text degradation after int4 quant. Not a large ppl jump but model inserts extra space before punctuation in multi-token emojis and sometimes drops trailing colon in YAML replies. Strange mix of vocab remap + rotary phase drift?
ben: can you attach a tiny repro and the conversion flags? which tokenizer mapping and headmap policy used?
nora: converted with `--vocab-map auto` and `--headmap rotate-compat`. quant: `qtool quant --mode int4 --backend avx-kernel --calib simple`. small failing prompt: `metadata:\n- name: service\n- port: 8080\n` expected colon preserved, got `port : 8080` or occasionally `port 8080` (colon dropped). also emoji sequence like "😊👍" becomes "😊 👍" (extra space).
shreya: colon dropping sounds like token boundary shift. emoji spacing is often due to tokenization differences (ZWJ/emoji sequences split). conversion's vocab-map might be merging tokens differently. Can you run `token-diff --check-emoji --check-zwj` between src and tgt?
ci-bot: token-diff output (summary): emoji-seq-preserved: false, zwj_tokens_changed: 3 tokens remapped, longest-run-shift: 2 token ids.
ben: that confirms tokenizer id shifts. But why punctuation spacing appears only after quant? suggests indexing or rotary alignment matter when decoding merges subword boundaries across softmax. two experiments: 1) preserve src vocab ids during quant (`--preserve-ids`) 2) run float rotary table while quantizing weights (`--preserve-rotary`).
li: also check kv-cache warmup: mismatched token ids can change prefix matches leading to different cache reuse and decode choices. run warmup with canonical prefixes for a few steps: `python warmup.py --model converted --prompts warmup_prompts.txt --repeat 5`
nora: quick runs: preserving ids yields colon preserved but BLEU roughly same; preserve-rotary reduces spaces around emojis by ~60%. combined preserve ids+rotary fixes the YAML colon case. looks like two interacting factors: token id remap causing different subtoken boundaries and rotary/quant noise amplifying decoder splice decisions.
shreya: thanks. action items: (1) add conversion check that flags emoji and zwj token remaps as high-risk, (2) add runtime warmup recommended step for converted models in docs, (3) add a small e2e test where we quantize but preserve rotary and run token-diff to ensure no boundary shifts. I'll open PRs for (1) and (3).
ben: I'll add a lightweight assert in the tokenizer wrapper that fails CI when `longest-run-shift > 1` on core tokens (punctuation, emoji, zwj).
ci-bot: created ticket #t-2026-77 assigned to nora/shreya/ben. priority: medium.
nora: final note: full 10k eval queued with preserve-rotary+preserve-ids. will update when done. Thanks all. :sparkles:
